rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since bodies equally admit every property, the sun’s distinctive illumination requires specification by a voluntary agent.
rows.anchor: كل ما يصح على أحد المثلين فإنه يصح أيضا على المثل الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Darkness is deprivation and light pure existence; night brings fear, sleep, and cessation, while dawn restores wakefulness, perception, and movement.
rows.anchor: أن الظلمة شبيهة بالعدم . بل البرهان القاطع قد دل على أنه مفهوم عدمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because light enables life, sensation, and movement, creating it is among God’s greatest blessings and proofs of power, mercy, and generosity.
rows.anchor: لما كان النور هو السبب الأصلي لحصول هذه الأحوال كان تأثير قدرة الله تعالى في تخليق النور من أعظم أقسام النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also reads the dawn splitting figuratively: God brings creation from nonexistence, life and reason from inertness, guidance from ignorance, and spiritual illumination from worldly darkness.
rows.anchor: فالق ظلمة العدم بصباح التكوين والإيجاد وفالق ظلمة الجمادية بصباح الحياة والعقل والرشاد

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth defines al-subh, al-sabah, and al-isbah as the beginning of day.
rows.anchor: قال الليث : الصبح والصباح هما أول النهار وهو الإصباح أيضا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses al-isbah in a line contrasting evening and morning, supporting its sense of morning.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر : أفنى رياحا وبنى رياح … تناسخ الإمساء والإصباح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation takes al-isbah as a verbal noun used as a name for morning.
rows.anchor: الإصباح } مصدر سمي به الصبح . فإن قيل : ظاهر الآية يدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation supplies an omitted darkness: God splits dawn’s darkness with dawn light, likened to opening a light channel through a sea of darkness in the eastern horizon.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد فالق ظلمة الإصباح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that God splits the morning light to produce the whiteness of day.
rows.anchor: كما يشق بحر الظلمة عن نور الصبح فكذلك يشق نور الصبح عن بياض النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation names the cause, splitting darkness, while intending its effect, the manifestation of dawn.
rows.anchor: أن ظهور النور في الصباح أنما كان لأجل أن الله تعالى فلق تلك الظلمة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say al-faliq means creator, so the phrase means creator of dawn.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : الفالق هو الخالق فكان المعنى خالق الإصباح

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf defines sakan as what a person finds reassuring and intimate, such as a spouse or beloved; fire is also called sakan because it offers company, and is called al-muʾnisa.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : السكن ما يسكن إليه الرجل ويطمئن إليه استئناسا به

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Night provides needed rest after daytime labor, so people can recover from exertion.
rows.anchor: ثم إن الليل يطمئن إليه الإنسان لأنه أتعب نفسه بالنهار واحتاج إلى زمان يستريح فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The absence of night in Paradise does not contradict its worldly benefit: the discussion concerns this world’s needs, while its customary conditions do not persist in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: كلامنا في أن الليل والنهار من ضروريات مصالح هذا العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asim and al-Kisaʾi read wajʿala as a verb; the others read jaʿil as an active participle. The participle suits the preceding active participles, while the verb governs the accusative sun and moon.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم والكسائي { وجعل اليل } على صيغة الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The active-participle reading parallels faliq al-habb and faliq al-isbah; the verbal reading supplies a governing verb for the accusative sun and moon.
rows.anchor: حجة من قرأ باسم الفاعل أن المذكور قبله اسم الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God set the sun’s cycle to a year and the moon’s to a month, organizing the seasons and the ripening of fruit and harvests; other speeds would disrupt these benefits.
rows.anchor: قدر حركة الشمس مخصوصة بمقدار من السرعة والبطء بحيث تتم الدورة في سنة

rows.speaker: أبو الهيثم
rows.claim: Abu al-Haytham takes husban as a plural of hisab, by analogy with other singular and plural pairs.
rows.anchor: قول أبي الهيثم أنه جمع حساب مثل ركاب وركبان وشهاب وشهبان

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf treats husban as a verbal noun, noting forms with both damma and kasra and comparing it with words such as kufran and ghufran.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : الحسبان بالضم مصدر حسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the sun and moon reckoned means setting them to a calculation, since times are known only through their orbits and courses.
rows.anchor: معنى جعل الشمس والقمر حسبانا جعلهما على حساب

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf reports three case readings: accusative by an understood verb, genitive coordinated with al-layl, or nominative as a subject with an omitted predicate meaning they are reckoned.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : { والشمس والقمر } قرئا بالحركات الثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aziz signals perfect power and al-Alim perfect knowledge: the celestial bodies’ specified properties and measured motions require comprehensive power and knowledge, proving they are specified by a willing agent rather than nature.
rows.anchor: والعزيز إشارة إلى كمال قدرته والعليم إشارة إلى كمال علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars are a third class of signs of divine power, mercy, and wisdom, created for people’s benefit.
rows.anchor: هذا هو النوع الثالث من الدلائل الدالة على كمال القدرة والرحمة والحكمة

words: لِتَهْتَدُوا۟ بِهَا فِى ظُلُمَٰتِ ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stars guide travelers on routes through dark land and sea when neither sun nor moon is visible.
rows.anchor: خلقها لتهتدي الخلق بها إلى الطرق والمسالك في ظلمات البر والبحر حيث لا يرون شمسا ولا قمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People use the sun’s movement to identify prayer times and daytime qibla, and the stars at night to identify the qibla.
rows.anchor: الناس يستدلون بأحوال حركة الشمس على معرفة أوقات الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elsewhere the Qurʾan says the stars adorn the heaven, citing 25:61, 37:6, and 85:1.
rows.anchor: كون هذه الكواكب زينة للسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars also serve as missiles against devils.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى ذكر في منافعها كونها رجوما للشياطين

words: لِتَهْتَدُوا۟ بِهَا فِى ظُلُمَٰتِ ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi offers a figurative reading: stars guide against the darkness of denying God’s voluntary agency and anthropomorphically assigning Him bodily location.
rows.anchor: المعطل ينفي كونه فاعلا مختارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their varied motion, position, brightness, and size show that identical bodies receive their properties by specification of a voluntary agent.
rows.anchor: نشاهد هذه الكواكب مختلفة في صفات كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stars are finite, composed, changing bodies; if these traits disqualify them as gods, God must be transcendent beyond body, parts, limits, place, and direction.
rows.anchor: وإن كانت عيوبا في الإلهية وجب تنزيه الإله عنها بأسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although this moves from the literal wording to metaphor, Razi says the interpretation closely suits the majesty of the Qurʾan.
rows.anchor: وهذا وإن كان عدولا عن حقيقة اللفظ إلى مجازه إلا أنه قريب مناسب لعظمة كتاب الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: The Sunni answer is that the detailed explanation is for those who know, comprehend, and understand, namely the believers.
rows.anchor: جواب أهل السنة : أن المراد منه كأنه تعالى يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars verse ends with yaʿlamun and the human-creation verse with yafqahun; creating humans from one source and varying their states is subtler workmanship, so fiqh signals greater insight and intelligence.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى ختم الآية السابقة ، وهي الآية التي استدل فيها بأحوال النجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of rain and vegetation is a fifth proof of God’s power, knowledge, wisdom, mercy, and beneficence toward creation.
rows.anchor: هذا النوع الخامس من الدلائل الدالة على كمال قدرة الله تعالى وعلمه وحكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These signs are also complete blessings; combining proof with beneficence strongly affects the heart, so callers to truth should use this approach.
rows.anchor: الدلائل كما أنها دلائل فهي أيضا نعم بالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi introduces the apparent implication that water descends from the sky and notes that people disagree about it.
rows.anchor: يقتضي نزول المطر من السماء

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi says God sends water from the sky to clouds, then from clouds to earth, retaining the apparent wording absent proof against it.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الجبائي في ( تفسيره ) : إنه تعالى ينزل الماء من السماء إلى السحاب

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Against the vapor account of rain, al-Jubbaʾi argues that hail in summer and liquid rain in the coldest weather contradict its explanation.
rows.anchor: احتج الجبائي على فساده من وجوه : الأول : أن البرد قد يوجد في وقت الحر

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: Proponents reply that summer heat drives cold into the vapor-rich cloud and concentrates it into hail, whereas winter cold outside prevents inner freezing so rain falls as water.
rows.anchor: القوم يجيبون عنه فيقولون : لا شك أن البخار أجزاء مائية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi counters that if the upper air is very cold, winter’s cold upper and lower air should prevent rain altogether, contrary to observation.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يجاب عنه بأن الطبقة العالية من الهواء باردة جدا عندكم

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi’s second argument says dispersed rising vapors cannot form droplets without a smooth continuous ceiling, such as glazed bathhouse roofs.
rows.anchor: الحجة الثانية : مما ذكره الجبائي أنه قال : إن البخارات إذا ارتفعت

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: The vapor proponents answer that cold air makes dispersed vapor heavy and descend; on a spherical world the particles converge and join into raindrops.
rows.anchor: القوم يجيبون عنه : بأن هذه البخارات إذا تصاعدت وتفرقت

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi’s third argument is that continuously rising sea vapors should cause continuous rainfall, which is not observed.
rows.anchor: الحجة الثالثة : ما ذكره الجبائي قال : لو كان تولد المطر

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi attributes the vapor theory to belief in eternal bodies, where events are only atoms acquiring new qualities, and each thing must arise from preexisting matter.
rows.anchor: والقوم إنما احتاجوا إلى هذا القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims hold that bodies are originated and the willing, powerful Creator makes them as He wills, removing the need for such strained natural explanations.
rows.anchor: وأما المسلمون . فلما اعتقدوا أن الأجسام محدثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other verses likewise say water or hail descends from the sky; Razi concludes God creates rain in the sky, then it descends through cloud to earth.
rows.anchor: جميع الآيات ناطقة بنزول المطر من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view takes the phrase to mean that rain is sent from the direction of the sky.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : المراد إنزال المطر من جانب السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view says water is sent from clouds, which God calls sky because Arabs use sky for anything above, as with a house ceiling.
rows.anchor: والقول الثالث : أنزل من السحاب ماء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi transmits from Ibn Abbas that the water here is rain and every raindrop is accompanied by an angel.
rows.anchor: نقل الواحدي في ( البسيط ) عن ابن عباس : يريد بالماء ههنا المطر

rows.speaker: الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Philosophers interpret the accompanying angel as the nature inherent in the body that causes its descent; Razi says a heavenly angel accompanying it is difficult to affirm.
rows.anchor: الفلاسفة يحملون ذلك الملك على الطبيعة الحالة في تلك الجسمية الموجبة لذلك النزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surface wording that God brings plants out by water implies natural causation, which theologians reject; Razi refers back to his discussion at 2:22.
rows.anchor: يدل على أنه تعالى إنما أخرج النبات بواسطة الماء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ restricts the phrase’s apparent universal meaning to plants of things that actually have plants; things without vegetation are excluded.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : قوله : { فأخرجنا به نبات كل شيء } ظاهره يقتضي أن يكون لكل شيء نبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing from the second-person address in anzala to the first-person plural in fa-akhrajna is iltifat; Razi says its rhetorical basis was treated at 10:22.
rows.anchor: يسمى التفاتا . ويعد ذلك من الفصاحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural form refers to God, who is one, by the convention that a great ruler speaks of himself in the plural.
rows.anchor: صيغة الجمع . والله واحد فرد لا شريك له

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says khadir means akhdar, green, with a shortened adjective form comparable to aʿwar and ʿawar.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : معنى خضر ، كمعنى أخضر

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth says khidr in the Qurʾan means grain crop, though in ordinary speech it can mean any green plant.
rows.anchor: قال الليث : الخضر في كتاب الله هو الزرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since 6:95 divides plants into what grows from grain and from date stones, Razi takes khadir here as the crop from grain, following al-Layth’s sense.
rows.anchor: اعتبر هذه القسمة أيضا في هذه الآية فابتدأ بذكر الزرع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the crops as wheat, barley, sult, maize, and rice, and khadir as the first green stalk with an ear at its top.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد القمح والشعير والسلت والذرة والأرز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stacked grains grow one above another in a single ear.
rows.anchor: يعني يخرج من ذلك الخضر حبا متراكبا بعضه على بعض في سنبلة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tiny sharp bodies above the ear are created to prevent birds from picking the stacked grains.
rows.anchor: ويحصل فوق السنبلة أجسام دقيقة حادة كأنها الأبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After plants from grain, the verse turns to the second category, plants from date stones: palms.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر ما ينبت من الحب أتبعه بذكر ما ينبت من النوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi reports an argument that mentioning grain crops before palms indicates crops are superior; al-Jahiz wrote a lengthy work on this question.
rows.anchor: أن الزرع أفضل من النخل

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says a palm produces its talʿ; the spathes are like cases before opening, and talʿ is the first visible part of a palm cluster, singular talʿa.
rows.anchor: روى الواحدي عن أبي عبيدة أنه قال : أطلعت النخل إذا أخرجت طلعها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says qinwan is the plural of qinw, like sunwan from sunw; its form resembles the dual, while the n-un inflection marks the plural.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : القنوان جمع قنو . مثل صنوان وصنو

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the near clusters as hanging palm bunches close enough to pick.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد العراجين التي قد تدلت من الطلع دانية ممن يجتنيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas takes them as short palms whose clusters cling close to the ground.
rows.anchor: وروى عنه أيضا أنه قال : قصار النخل اللاصقة عذوقها بالأرض

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that distant bunches are omitted because mentioning one of two opposites implies the other, as in garments protecting from heat without naming cold.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : ولم يقل ومنها قنوان بعيدة لأن ذكر أحد القسمين يدل على الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation singles out near bunches because their closeness makes the blessing greater and more abundant.
rows.anchor: وقيل أيضا : ذكر الدانية في القريبة

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf parses qinwan as a nominative subject with min al-nakhl as predicate and min talʿiha as apposition; alternatively its predicate is omitted and inferred from akhrajna.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) { قنوان } رفع بالابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For readers who have yukhraju minhu habb, qinwan is coordinated with habb; qinwan is also read with qaf either damma or fatha as a collective noun.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ يخرج منه { حب } كان { طلعها قنوان } عنده

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Asim, also reported as Ali’s reading, has nominative jannat; the others read it in the accusative, with differing syntactic explanations.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم : { جنات } بضم التاء ، وهي قراءة علي رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative may mean gardens are alongside the palms or coordinate with qinwan as what is produced; the accusative coordinates with نبات كل شيء, while al-Kashshaf prefers specification for the especially fine olives and pomegranates.
rows.anchor: أما القراءة الأولى فلها وجهان : الأول : أن يراد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says olive and pomegranate refer to their trees, as ask the village means ask its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : قوله : { والزيتون والرمان } يريد شجر الزيتون
